title: Complete Remaining Ledger Domain-to-ORM Mappers
objective: Complete all remaining explicit Ledger Domain-to-ORM mappers, frozen ChangedFile/ChangedSymbol technical identities, eleven-object round trips, and drift verification without adding persistence runtime.
scope: RunRelationship, ChangedFile, ChangedSymbol, TestExecution, ImplementationArtifact, ComponentReference, ArchitectureDecisionReference, Limitation, and RecommendedTask bidirectional mapping.
Frozen technical-ID algorithms, reverse identity verification, explicit parent Run validation, safe errors, round trips, field/Enum/inventory drift and purity guards.
Complete Mapper contract, bounded Context/Project Memory updates, Implementation Run, full relevant regression, and one local commit.
explicit_non_goals: No PostgreSQL Repository, Session, Unit of Work, database schema creation, migration execution, or real PostgreSQL verification.
No Manifest Parser/Indexer, repository identity resolver, Git consistency service, API, UI, Repository replay/conflict/cycle/transaction behavior, or dynamic reflection Mapper.
No Domain/ORM table/accepted ADR/dependency/lockfile/runtime configuration/Factor Lab/TDX/Dataset Snapshot/Factor DSL/Optimization/Validation/Registry/LightGBM/Qlib change and no push.

known_limitations: No Manifest Parser/Indexer or trusted logical repository identity binding exists.
No PostgreSQL Repository, Session, Unit of Work, migration, deployed schema/tables, or real database verification exists.
Mapper and technical-identity versions are not persisted in ORM columns.
ImplementationArtifact retains the frozen Domain scheme-prefix location semantics.
unresolved_questions: How will migration invocation, ordering, checksum tracking, rollback, and schema privileges work?
Which isolated PostgreSQL fixture and CI capability will verify the migration?
How will a future Indexer bind logical repository identity and persist Mapper/identity versions?
How will the production Repository translate immutable, expected-version, and graph conflicts?
rollback_information: Revert the single containing commit. No database, schema, migration, data, API, dependency, lockfile, runtime configuration, business module, or Factor Lab rollback is required.
security_impact: Mapper errors expose only stable safe metadata and omit arbitrary records, commands, descriptions, reasons, credentials, filesystem content, and URLs; no external system was accessed.
data_lineage_impact: No research or database data changed. Deterministic complete Mapper semantics and technical-ID verification now exist, but no durable Ledger indexing or Manifest binding occurred.
